claim_text: 2Co- and 5Co-MBG keep an ordered mesoporous channel structure (pores ~4-5 nm)

steps.observation: Small-angle XRD: one low-angle reflection in all three patterns, at 2theta ~1.37 (MBG), ~1.47 (2Co) and ~1.35 deg (5Co)
steps.image_note: linked text gives 2theta 1.25-1.30 deg; plotted peaks sit at ~1.35-1.5 deg

panels.caption_span: Fig. 2. Small-angle XRD analysis for MBG, 2Co-MBG and 5Co-MBG scaffolds.
panels.layer_why: saturation split caught the whole layer; clean panel handed over, masked regions declared

steps.contribution_why: A single low-angle XRD reflection in each pattern indicates some periodic mesostructure (a characteristic d-spacing) in MBG, 2Co-MBG and 5Co-MBG, but one peak alone does not establish the pore diameter (~4-5 nm) or confirm a channel (e.g., hexagonal) pore geometry, which would require additional peak indexing or complementary data like TEM/nitrogen sorption.
unsettled: channel/hexagonal pore geometry versus other ordered arrangements
long-range order beyond a single reflection (higher-order peaks)

steps.observation: Low-angle peak height falls ~8-fold with Co: ~180000 (MBG), ~74000 (2Co), ~23000 (5Co), 5Co peak barely above the rising background
steps.image_note: linked text calls all three peaks 'obvious'

panels.caption_span: Fig. 2. Small-angle XRD analysis for MBG, 2Co-MBG and 5Co-MBG scaffolds.
panels.layer_why: saturation split caught the whole layer; clean panel handed over, masked regions declared

steps.contribution_why: The steep ~8-fold drop in low-angle XRD peak intensity, with the 5Co peak barely rising above background, indicates a substantial loss of long-range mesopore ordering rather than a preserved ordered channel structure, which undermines the claim especially for 5Co-MBG.
unsettled: actual pore diameter (~4-5 nm) confirmation via TEM or N2 sorption
whether 2Co retains sufficient order despite reduced peak height
whether the intensity drop reflects loss of order vs. reduced scattering contrast/wall thickness changes

steps.observation: TEM: parallel channel stripes over ~200 nm in a and a regular pore lattice in b, period ~5-6 nm
steps.image_note: packet F4 is paper Fig. 3; pore diameter alone is not resolvable from wall at this scale; MBG not imaged

panels.layer_why: only OCR text boxes could be found, and hiding words while arrows or marks remain is forbidden; panel handed over whole and declared

panels.caption_span: scaffolds. They have well-ordered mesopore channel structure with a pore size around 4.5-5nm
panels.layer_why: only OCR text boxes could be found, and hiding words while arrows or marks remain is forbidden; panel handed over whole and declared

steps.contribution_why: The TEM images show ordered channel stripes and a regular pore lattice consistent with an ordered mesoporous structure, and the ~5-6 nm period is close to the claimed ~4-5 nm pore size, but the observation does not explicitly confirm that panels a and b correspond specifically to the 2Co- and 5Co-MBG samples nor pin the pore size precisely to the 4-5 nm range.
unsettled: explicit identification of panel a and b as 2Co-MBG and 5Co-MBG specifically
exact pore size match to 4-5 nm versus measured ~5-6 nm
whether ordering is uniform across the whole sample beyond the ~200 nm imaged region

steps.observation: N2 isotherms of all three show a hysteresis step at P/P0 ~0.45-0.6 (type IV)

panels.layer_why: saturation split caught the whole layer; clean panel handed over, masked regions declared

steps.contribution_why: The type IV isotherm with H1/H2-type hysteresis at P/P0 ~0.45-0.6 is characteristic of capillary condensation in uniform mesopores and thus evidences a mesoporous structure common to all three samples, but the isotherm shape alone does not pin down the specific pore diameter (~4-5 nm, which requires BJH/pore-size-distribution analysis) or confirm long-range structural order of the channels (typically shown by XRD or TEM).
unsettled: long-range ordering of the channel structure
that 2Co- and 5Co-MBG specifically (as opposed to the third sample) retain this structure

closing_why: the claim names a fact no panel carries: TEM panel a = 2Co-MBG, b = 5Co-MBG (caption); pore size 4.5-5 nm from caption
